excerpt: Loft is a São Paulo proptech for buying, selling and renting homes, with home-loan and rental-guarantee services. Founders, funding, the 2022 layoffs and alternatives.
content:
Loft is a Brazilian real estate technology company based in São Paulo. TechCrunch described it in 2021 as a digital platform aiming to be a one-stop shop for buying and selling homes: a marketplace of listings worked by brokers, plus services in insurance, renovations, rentals and mortgages. It started as an iBuyer that bought apartments directly, then moved into mortgages in 2020 by acquiring a large Brazilian mortgage brokerage. At that time it listed more than 13,000 properties across about 130 regions of São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro and worked with more than 30,000 brokers.

Loft was founded in early 2018 by Mate Pencz and Florian Hagenbuch, who served as co-CEOs and had previously built and sold the Brazilian printing startup Printi. It grew quickly through acquisitions: Bloomberg Línea lists CredPago (rental leases without a guarantor), CrediHome (home-loan origination), Foxter, the condominium portal 123i, the real estate software company Vista, and Mexico City's TrueHome, which became Loft Mexico.

It also raised large sums. In March 2021 Loft raised a $425 million Series D led by D1 Capital Partners at a $2.2 billion valuation, with investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Tiger Global, Altimeter and Soros, TechCrunch reported; a $100 million extension in April 2021 lifted its valuation to $2.9 billion. Total equity funding reached about $800 million.

As Brazilian interest rates rose, Loft cut staff. TechCrunch reported about 380 layoffs in July 2022, after 159 in April, and Bloomberg Línea reported a further 312 in December 2022, about 12% of its roughly 2,600 staff, which it linked to integrating acquired companies. Loft denied a report that it had raised money at a lower valuation and said it had not raised equity since mid-2021, and that its products and services continued unchanged.

Loft does not charge buyers to browse listings; brokerage, loan and rental-guarantee costs depend on each transaction. Its website blocked our checks, so we could not confirm current fees.

This page is research, not a review. Facts come from the reporting listed under Sources.
